label: Clickhouse
description: Tools to query and explore a ClickHouse database

tools.name: ListColumns
tools.description:
Get the schema/structure of a ClickHouse table in the ClickHouse database
when the schema is not known, and the name of the table is provided.

This tool should ALWAYS be used before executing any query.
All tables in the query must be discovered first,
so that their exact names are known.

parameters.name: schema_name
parameters.description: The schema to get the table schema of

parameters.name: table_name
parameters.description: The table to get the schema of

tools.name: ListDatabases
tools.description: Discover all the databases in the ClickHouse database.

output.description: The databases on the ClickHouse server

tools.name: ListSchemas
tools.description:
Discover all the schemas in the ClickHouse database.

Note: ClickHouse doesn't have schemas like PostgreSQL, so this returns a default schema name.

output.description: The schemas in the ClickHouse database

tools.name: ListTables
tools.description:
Discover all the tables in the ClickHouse database when the list of tables is not known.

ALWAYS use this tool before any other tool that requires a table name.

output.description: The tables in the default database

tools.name: QueryRows
tools.description:
You have a connection to a ClickHouse database.
Execute a SELECT query and return the results against the ClickHouse database.
No other queries (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, etc.) are allowed.

ONLY use this tool if you have already loaded the schema of the tables you need to query.

The final query will be constructed as follows:
SELECT {select_query_part} FROM {from_clause} JOIN {join_clause}
WHERE {where_clause} HAVING {having_clause}
ORDER BY {order_by_clause} LIMIT {limit} OFFSET {offset}

When running queries, follow these rules which will help avoid errors:
* Never "select *" from a table. Always select the columns you need.
* Always order your results. Use the most important columns or the primary key if you're unsure.
* Always use case-insensitive queries to match strings in the query.
* Always trim strings in the query.
* Prefer LIKE queries over direct string matches or regex queries.
* Only join on columns that are indexed or the primary key. Do not join on arbitrary columns.
* ClickHouse is case-sensitive, so be careful with table and column names.

parameters.name: select_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the SELECT keyword with a comma separated list of columns you wish to return. Do not include the SELECT keyword.

parameters.name: from_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the FROM keyword. Do not include the FROM keyword.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of rows to return. This is the LIMIT clause of the query. Defaults to 100.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The number of rows to skip. This is the OFFSET clause of the query. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: join_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the JOIN keyword. Do not include the JOIN keyword. Defaults to no JOIN clause.

parameters.name: where_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the WHERE keyword. Do not include the WHERE keyword. Defaults to no WHERE clause.

parameters.name: having_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the HAVING keyword. Do not include the HAVING keyword. Defaults to no HAVING clause.

parameters.name: group_by_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the GROUP BY keyword. Do not include the GROUP BY keyword. Defaults to no GROUP BY clause.

parameters.name: order_by_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the ORDER BY keyword. Do not include the ORDER BY keyword. Defaults to no ORDER BY clause.

parameters.name: with_clause
parameters.description: This is the part of the SQL query that comes after the WITH keyword when basing the query on a virtual table. Defaults to no WITH clause.

select_clause.value: user_id, trim(user_name) AS user_name, email, created_at, total_orders

with_clause.value: ranked_users AS (SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders FROM orders GROUP BY user_id)

summary:
The Clickhouse toolkit for Arcade connects to a ClickHouse database and enables agents to explore its structure and query its data via a structured, read-only interface.

## Capabilities

- **Schema discovery**: List all databases, schemas (returns a default placeholder, as ClickHouse lacks PostgreSQL-style schemas), tables, and column-level structure before executing any query.
- **Read-only querying**: Execute `SELECT` statements with explicit support for filtering, joining (on indexed/primary-key columns), ordering, pagination (`LIMIT`/`OFFSET`), and aggregation (`HAVING`). Write operations (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`) are not permitted.
- **Query safety guardrails**: Built-in rules enforce column-explicit selects, case-insensitive string matching, string trimming, `LIKE`-based matching, and indexed-only joins to reduce runtime errors.

## Secrets

`CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`

A ClickHouse connection string that encodes the host, port, database name, username, and password needed to reach your ClickHouse instance. The exact format depends on your client driver (e.g., `clickhouse://user:password@host:port/database` for HTTP-based clients). Obtain the values from your ClickHouse deployment:

- **ClickHouse Cloud**: Navigate to your service in the [ClickHouse Cloud console](https://clickhouse.cloud/), click **Connect**, and copy the connection details shown for your preferred client.
- **Self-hosted**: Use the host/port configured in your `config.xml` (default HTTP port `8123`, native port `9000`), along with the credentials of a user that has at minimum `SELECT` and `SHOW` privileges on the target database.

Ensure the user account has read-only access restricted to the intended database to limit exposure.

For guidance on storing secrets in Arcade, see the [Arcade secrets documentation](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets). You can manage secret values at [https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets).
